changelog:
Important: first version with signed updates. Sites running 0.2.0-beta.25 receive it from Dashboard > Updates with data and settings kept; from this version on, the plugin accepts an update from aiframe.it only when its update file is signed with one of the keys it ships.
Security: one visitor can start at most a quarter of the site's daily AI requests (at least 20). Past that, this visitor gets the contact form and the other visitors keep getting answers.
Security: per-visitor limits count IPv6 addresses by /64 network, so changing address inside one network no longer avoids them.
Security: after 50 request emails in a day, new contact requests are still saved and listed as not delivered, but no more emails are sent; the owner can resend them from the Requests page.
Security: updates from aiframe.it are accepted only when the update file carries a valid Ed25519 signature of the version, the package address and its SHA-256. The signing key is not stored on that server. (The WordPress.org package has no update checker and is not affected.)
Security: the contact form has server-side limits (name cut to 80 characters, email over 200 refused) and a hidden honeypot field; a request that fills it is acknowledged but neither saved nor emailed. Links written by the visitor are shown as [link] in the owner email; the saved request keeps the original text.
Security: the preview link sets a cookie and reloads the page without the token, so it does not stay in the address bar, history or server logs; the widget sends it in a header.
Security: public chat replies no longer include the diagnostic code; it stays in test mode and for administrators.
Security: uninstalling on a multisite network removes the plugin data of every site, not only the current one.
New: Settings > AI provider warns when the API key is saved in the database while the WordPress salts are in the database too, and suggests the wp-config.php constants.
Changed: within one chat question each source is split and indexed once, so rephrased searches cost almost nothing; the monthly cap check is a single total per model and runs no query when the cap is 0. The widget no longer sends the page address and UTM codes, which the plugin did not use.
Fixed: backslashes in settings texts (for example in the welcome message) are kept when saving.
New: the initial check has a sixth item, Visitor addresses. It warns when the site is behind a CDN or a reverse proxy and no trusted proxy is set. Settings > Network shows the same warning and the address the plugin sees for the administrator.
